1 The diagram shows a Bunsen burner.
(a) The Bunsen burner uses methane as a fuel.
Methane has the formula $ \mathrm{C H_{4}} $
Give the names of the two elements in methane.
(b) When methane burns it reacts with a gas in the air. Give the name of this gas.
(c) (i) Name the two substances that form when methane burns in plenty of air.
(ii) Name the poisonous gas that forms when methane burns in a shortage of air.
(Total for Question 1 = 6 marks)
2 A student uses this apparatus to investigate the burning of four different liquid fuels, W, X, Y and Z.
The table shows the student's results.
Fuel | Initial temperature in℃ | Final temperature in℃ | Increase in temperature in℃
W | 19.0 | 31.3 | 12.3
X | 18.4 | 28.7 | 
Y | 19.5 | 35.4 |

(a) Complete the table by giving the increase in temperature for fuels X, Y and Z.
(b) The student uses the same mass of water and burns each fuel for the same period of time. Explain which fuel releases the most heat energy.
(c) What is the name given to reactions that release heat energy?
A decomposition
B endothermic
C exothermic
D reduction
(Total for Question 2 = 4 marks)

5 Ethanol can be manufactured by fermentation or by the direct hydration of ethene.
(a) In Brazil, the main source of sugar for fermentation is sugar cane.
sugar cane is added to water
sugar cane contains sucrose $ \left( \mathrm{C}_{1 2} \mathrm{H}_{2 2} \mathrm{O}_{1 1} \right) $ that dissolves in the water

during the fermentation process the sucrose is broken down into glucose $ \left( \mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{1 2} \mathrm{O}_{6} \right) $
this glucose is then converted into ethanol （ $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{5} O H} $ ）and carbon dioxide
(i) Name the substance that is added to the sucrose solution to allow fermentation to take place.
(ii) Complete the equation for the conversion of sucrose into glucose.
\mathrm {C} _ {1 2} \mathrm {H} _ {2 2} \mathrm {O} _ {1 1} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow
(iii) Write a chemical equation for the conversion of glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.
(iv) Fermentation produces a solution that is a mixture of ethanol and water.
Which of these is the most effective method of obtaining ethanol from this mixture?
A crystallisation
B filtration
C fractional distillation
D simple distillation
(b) In the direct hydration method, ethene reacts with steam.
The equation for the reaction is
\mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {4} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {5} \mathrm {O H}
(i) Name the catalyst used in this reaction.
(ii) State the temperature and pressure used in this reaction.

temperature
pressure
(c) This apparatus is used to convert ethanol into ethene.
(i) Name the type of reaction taking place.
(ii) State the function of the aluminium oxide in this reaction.
(d) Ethene belongs to a homologous series of unsaturated hydrocarbons called alkenes.
(i) State what is meant by the term unsaturated.
(ii) State the colour change that is observed when bromine water is shaken with ethene in a test tube.

6 Phosgene $ \left( \mathrm{C O C I}_{2} \right) $ is used in industry to make polymers.
(a) Phosgene is formed when carbon monoxide reacts with chlorine.
\mathrm {C O} (\mathrm {g}) + \mathrm {C I} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm {C O C I} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \quad \Delta H = - 1 0 8 \mathrm {k J / m o l}
(i) The reaction mixture is kept at temperatures between 50 and $ 1 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ If a temperature above $ 2 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ is used, only a small amount of phosgene is formed.
Suggest why only a small amount of phosgene is formed at temperatures above 200 $ ^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $

(ii) Predict how the yield of phosgene will change if the reaction is carried out at a higher pressure.
Give a reason for your answer. [assume the reaction reaches a position of equilibrium]
(b) Phosgene reacts with water to form hydrochloric acid and carbon dioxide. Write a chemical equation for this reaction.
(c) The diagram shows the displayed formula of phosgene.
Draw a dot and cross diagram to show the arrangement of all the outer electrons in a molecule of phosgene.
7 Magnesium carbonate decomposes when heated to form magnesium oxide and carbon dioxide. The equation for the reaction is
\mathrm {M g C O} _ {3} (\mathrm {s}) \rightarrow \mathrm {M g O} (\mathrm {s}) + \mathrm {C O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})
A student uses this method to investigate the reaction.
Step1 weigh a clean, dry crucible and record the mass
Step 2 add some magnesium carbonate
Step 3 reweigh the crucible and contents and record the new mass
Step 4 heat the crucible and contents for five minutes
Step 5 allow the crucible and contents to cool and then reweigh
Step 6 repeat steps 4 and 5 until the mass of the crucible and contents does not change
The student does the experiment four times.

The table shows her results.
| Mass in g
 | Experiment 1 | Experiment 2 | Experiment 3 | Experiment 4
mass of empty crucible | 19.20 | 21.31 | 19.83 | 20.45
mass of crucible and magnesium carbonate before heating | 23.40 | 24.94 | 24.65 | 26.92
mass of crucible and contents after heating for 5 minutes | 22.85 | 23.21 | 22.13 | 24.02
mass of crucible and contents after heating for a total of 10 minutes | 21.94 | 23.04 | 22.13 | 23.53
mass of crucible and contents after heating for a total of 15 minutes | 21.60 | 23.04 | 22.13 | 23.53
(a) State why the mass of the crucible and contents decreases during heating.
(b) (i) State the reason for Step 6.
(ii) Explain in which experiment the student should have heated for a fourth period of five minutes.
(Total for Question 7 = 4 marks)

8 Acid indigestion is caused by having too much hydrochloric acid in the stomach.
A suspension of magnesium hydroxide, $ \mathrm{M g(OH)}_{2} $ , in water, can be used to cure acid indigestion.
The equation for the reaction between magnesium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid is

\mathrm {M g} (\mathrm {O H}) _ {2} (\mathrm {s}) + 2 \mathrm {H C l} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {M g C l} _ {2} (\mathrm {a q}) + 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {I})
A student investigates how much magnesium hydroxide is needed to neutralise $ 1 0 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of hydrochloric acid with a concentration of $ 0. 0 9 6 8 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3}. $
He uses 0.29g of magnesium hydroxide to neutralise the hydrochloric acid.
(a) Calculate the amount, in moles, of HCl in the hydrochloric acid.
amount of HCl
(b) Calculate the amount, in moles, of $ \mathrm{M g(OH)}_{2} $ used by the student. $ [M_{r} $ of $ \mathrm{M g(OH)}_{2}=5 8] $
\mathrm {M g} (\mathrm {O H}) _ {2}
(c) Explain whether the student used the right amount of magnesium hydroxide to neutralise the hydrochloric acid.
(Total for Question 8 = 6 marks)
9 The flow chart shows the steps in the manufacture of sulfuric acid.
(a) The equation for the reaction in step 2 is
\mathrm {S O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) + \frac {1}{2} \mathrm {O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm {S O} _ {3} (\mathrm {g}) \quad \Delta H = - 9 6 \mathrm {k J / m o l}

(i) State what the symbols $ \rightleftharpoons $ and $ \Delta H $ represent.
$ \Delta H. $
(ii) Name the catalyst used in step 2.
(iii) State the temperature and pressure used in the reaction in step 2.
temperature
pressure.
(b) Sulfur trioxide reacts with water to form sulfuric acid. This reaction is very exothermic.
\mathrm {S O} _ {3} (\mathrm {g}) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {l}) \rightarrow \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {S O} _ {4} (\mathrm {a q}) \quad \Delta H = - 2 2 8 \mathrm {k J / m o l}
(i) State why the sulfur trioxide is not dissolved in water to form sulfuric acid in step 3.
(ii) Write chemical equations for the reactions that take place in step 3 and step 4.
(c) Give two industrial uses for sulfuric acid.
(Total for Question 9 = 10 marks)
